title: State Tax Withholding Schedule for Income Annuities Commuted Value Payments
content:
State tax is withheld from a commuted value paid on an Ashgrove Income Annuities contract only when federal tax is withheld from it and federal tax was withheld from the contract's installments falling due in the twelve months before the payment — that is, the federal tax withheld on installments issued for payment dates in those twelve months totals more than zero.

When both conditions hold, the state of issue decides the rate, applied to the taxable part and rounded to the cent:

- Iowa, Minnesota, North Carolina or Vermont — the state flat rate, **5% (0.05)**;
- Delaware, New York or Oklahoma — the alternative state rate, **4% (0.04)**.

Otherwise no state tax is withheld from the commuted value.

| State of issue | Federal tax on the lump sum | Federal tax on installments due in the prior twelve months | State tax |
|---|---|---|---|
| North Carolina | Withheld | Withheld | 5% of the taxable part |
| Oklahoma | Withheld | Withheld | 4% of the taxable part |
| Oklahoma | Withheld | None | None |
| Vermont | None (0% chosen) | Withheld | None |
| Arizona | Withheld | Withheld | None |

*Hypothetical figure.* Taxable part $41,323.78 on a Vermont contract with both conditions met: $2,066.189, so $2,066.19 of state tax.
